kurz: Sour usually means too little was extracted, bitter too much: grind size, brewing time and water temperature decide.
bild_im_kopf: Like a teabag taken out too early or too late: the good moment lies in between.

ursachen.titel: Ground too coarse or brewed too briefly
ursachen.warum: Acids dissolve first. If brewing stops too early, sweetness and body are missing and the acidity stands out.

ursachen.titel: Ground too fine or brewed too long
ursachen.warum: The bitter compounds dissolve last. Too fine a grind or too long a contact time pulls them out.
Below about 90 °C the water dissolves too little; water at a rolling boil quickly pulls out bitterness. About 92–96 °C works well (as a guide).
fix: Use water just off the boil

q1.frage: Is the coffee more bitter than sour?

q2.frage: Do you grind very fine or brew longer than usual?
